items.title: Sabarimala halal jaggery row: Kerala High Court tells Devaswom Board to exercise greater care
items.summary: The Kerala High Court on Tuesday told the Travancore Devaswom Board (TDB) to exercise greater care while procuring supplies for making Nivedyam/ Prasadam at the Sabarimala temple after a plea raised objections to the use of halal certified jaggery in the preparations [SJR Kumar v The Travancore Devaswom Board & ors]. A Division Bench of Justices Raja Vijayaraghavan V and KV Jayakumar said that the board should have ensured that the supplies for the temple did not carry symbols or declaration that could create concerns over whether the materials complied with the religious customs followed at Sabarimala. " Ideally, the Travancore Devaswom Board ought to have exercised greater care to ensure that the quantity of jaggery supplied by the manufacturer did not bear symbols, markings or declarations that could give rise to an apprehension of conflict with the religious customs and practices followed at the Temple, " the Court added. The Court, however, found no issue with the quality of the jaggery as the laboratory reports showed that it was satisfactory and did not contain any substance or element that made it unsuitable for preparing Prasadam.
